title: Stepwells of North Gujarat
summary: A two-week expedition tracing how water architecture evolved from the Chaulukya temple tank at Modhera to the Sultanate-era vavs of Ahmedabad, recorded in Hindi and Gujarati field notes.

stops.narrative: Started at dawn at Adalaj, where the light falls through the octagonal openings into the lower galleries.
Found the twin inscriptions in Sanskrit and Arabic and photographed both for transcription.
Sketched the Surya Kund: a stepped tank that shares its vocabulary with the stepwells.
Two days at Rani ki Vav counting sculptures gallery by gallery.
Ended with the Salvi weavers of Patan, whose double-ikat patterns echo the stepwell's geometry.

title: Kutch Crafts Trail
summary: Living heritage after the 2001 earthquake: palaces under repair, craft villages rebuilt, and the Harappan city that once mastered the same desert's water.

stops.narrative: Began in Bhuj at the Aina Mahal, still carrying the scars of the 2001 earthquake.
Spent a day with Ajrakh printers, following one cloth through its many dye baths.
Watched Rogan painting and copper bell-making in Nirona.
Crossed the Rann to Dholavira to study its reservoirs.

title: Baolis of the North
summary: From a Delhi baoli wrapped in ghost stories to the vertiginous geometry of Abhaneri and a Jodhpur jhalra brought back to life.

stops.narrative: Collected stories about the baoli's 'black water' from Old Delhi residents.
Measured shadows across the thirteen storeys of Chand Baori.
Ended at Toorji ka Jhalra, restored and full of life again.
